title: Front Desk: Hotel Check-In
shared_passage:
Listen to a woman checking into a hotel, and for questions 1 to 7, choose the correct answer.

RECEPTIONIST: Good evening. Welcome to Saint John's Manor Hotel. How can I help you?

WOMAN: Hi, I have a reservation under the name Lisa Berardelli.

RECEPTIONIST: Let me check. Lisa Berardelli. How do you spell that?

WOMAN: B-E-R-A-R-D-E-DOUBLE L-I.

RECEPTIONIST: Thank you, Ms. Berardelli. I see a reservation for a twin room for two nights.

WOMAN: Actually, I booked a single room for one night.

RECEPTIONIST: I'm terribly sorry. I was looking at a different reservation. Let me find the correct one. Ah, here it is—a single room for one night.

WOMAN: No problem.

RECEPTIONIST: May I please see some ID?

WOMAN: Sure, here's my passport.

RECEPTIONIST: Thank you. Breakfast is included and is served from 7 am to 10 am in the dining area.

WOMAN: Great, thanks. Can I have dinner at the restaurant this evening?

RECEPTIONIST: I'm afraid we don't have any tables available this evening, but you can order room service. Just dial 0 to talk to the reception desk.

WOMAN: OK, thank you.

RECEPTIONIST: Here is your key card and the Wi-Fi password. Check-out time is 11 am.

WOMAN: Is it possible to do a late check-out?

RECEPTIONIST: Unfortunately, that's not possible, but you can leave your luggage at reception and check out at 12.

WOMAN: That works. Thank you.

RECEPTIONIST: Is there anything else you need?

WOMAN: Yes, actually. My phone is running out of battery, and I forgot my charger. Can I request a wake-up call?

RECEPTIONIST: Of course, no problem. What time would you like the call?

WOMAN: At 7:00 am, please. Um, actually, make it 7:30.

RECEPTIONIST: Of course.

WOMAN: Thanks.

RECEPTIONIST: You're welcome. If you need anything else, just let us know. Have a pleasant stay.

WOMAN: Thank you, goodnight.

options: The computer didn't show a reservation
